audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Karma 6 of 7 stages and Rumble none, while the data says Rumble wins 52.3% over 1914 games.
audit.why: Karma genuinely owns levels 1-5 on range, so most of the chart is right. What is missing is the resolution: she drifts into enchanter utility while Rumble's AP burn scales, which is where a 52.3% comes from. Giving the 2+ items stage to Rumble reconciles the chart with the data and with the page's own late-game text, without inventing an early-game shift.
audit.corrected: win[6] Karma -> Rumble, with whys[6] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mantra's cooldown appears nowhere, and the level-6 spike says neither champion gains anything.
audit.why: Mantra is 40/38/36/34 and is available from level 1 — it is the real spike clock in this lane, not level 6. Gathering Fire shortens it every time one of her damaging abilities lands, so free poke is literally her ultimate charging. A Rumble who knows Mantra is 40 seconds knows exactly how long his window is after she spends it.
audit.corrected: Mantra's 40s and Gathering Fire added to the spike and mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places call her root 'RQ' / 'Mantra-Q root-tether'.
audit.why: Mantra-Q is Inner Flame plus a delayed cataclysm — pure damage, no root. The root is Focused Resolve (W), and Mantra-W is what extends it and heals her. Telling a player to fear a root from the wrong ability means they dodge the wrong thing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tether break is never stated, even though the full layer already knows it.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a 675-range tether that only roots if it holds. Leaving the radius or breaking line of sight cancels it — and Scrap Shield's move-speed burst is exactly the tool for that. The full layer says 'breaks if you LoS / outrange it'; the content layer never told the player.
audit.corrected: State the 675 radius and the break condition, and point Scrap Shield at it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'wait for it to expire (roughly 4 seconds)' for Inspire.
audit.why: Inspire's shield duration is not something the data supports, but its cooldown is: 10/9.5/9/8.5/8. Quoting the cooldown makes the same advice concrete and true.

edits.before: Two-item Karma has enough AP to one-rotate you if Scrap Shield is down — play for Equalizer teamfight impact rather than trying to win a 1v1 you lost all lane.
edits.after: Two items in she drifts toward enchanter utility while your burn keeps scaling — you still lose the duel she owned all lane, but the teamfight, and the matchup, turn yours.

edits.before: Her Level 2 W-tether root means any step-up attempt risks a root-into-full-combo; she controls the trade completely.
edits.after: Focused Resolve tethers at 675 and roots only if it holds — leave that radius or break line of sight and no root ever lands.

edits.before: RQ root-tether you when Scrap Shield is on cooldown, then Q-poke the follow-up freely
edits.after: Mantra-W root you while Scrap Shield is down, then Inner Flame the follow-up freely

edits.before: Bait her Mantra charge on a minion or bad angle, then close fast with double Electro-Harpoon slow
edits.after: Bait Mantra out — it is 40s at rank 1 — then close on the slow from a double Electro Harpoon

edits.before: Neither of you gains a new combat tool at 6, but your Equalizer threat forces her to play back from river — the one window you can use to push and roam.
edits.after: Neither of you gains a new button at 6, but The Equalizer forces her off the river, and every Mantra she spends buys you up to 40 seconds to push and roam.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the worst stretch of this lane. Karma's Mantra-Q is a slow-field burst that hits for a third of your HP, and she can shield herself with E then kite your every Flamespitter with the movement-speed bonus — you simply cannot stick to her without landing Electro-Harpoon first. Your pattern is: bait the E shield by walking up, wait for it to expire (roughly 4 seconds), then double-harpoon the slow and walk in with Danger Zone Flamespitter. If she burns Mantra on a bad angle, that is your punish window. At Level 6 neither of you gains a new button, but your Equalizer changes the map — drop it perpendicular to her escape route any time she overextends, and the slow-field forces the trade she does not want. Respect her RQ root-tether if Scrap Shield is down; that tether into your own team is a fast death.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the worst stretch of this lane. Mantra-Q is a delayed cataclysm that hits for a third of your HP, and Inspire's shield plus move speed kites your Flamespitter — you cannot stick to her without landing Electro Harpoon first. Your pattern is: bait Inspire by walking up, count its 10 seconds at rank 1, then double-harpoon the slow and walk in with Danger Zone Flamespitter. Gathering Fire shortens Mantra every time one of her spells lands, so free poke is her ultimate charging; if she spends Mantra badly you own the next 40 seconds. At Level 6 The Equalizer changes the map — drop it perpendicular to her escape route when she overextends. Her root is Focused Resolve, not Mantra-Q: leave the 675 tether or break line of sight and it never locks.

edits.before: Late game Karma drifts into an enchanter-utility role but RQ never stops being a threat — two items of AP makes it genuinely burst-level damage. Your Equalizer remains your strongest asset: in teamfights a well-placed Equalizer wall is worth more than winning the 1v1 you were losing all lane. Look for flanks where she cannot E-speed out of the zone in time, and save Scrap Shield for her RQ burst rather than for minion chip. If you are even or ahead in gold, your sustained Danger Zone Flamespitter in a narrow corridor will out-damage her poke cycle; if you are behind, play for Equalizer and let your team close.
edits.after: Late game Karma drifts into an enchanter-utility role but Mantra-Q never stops being a threat — two items of AP makes it genuinely burst-level damage. The Equalizer remains your strongest asset: in teamfights a well-placed line is worth more than the 1v1 you were losing all lane. Look for flanks where Inspire's move speed cannot carry her out of the burn in time, and spend Scrap Shield on breaking a Focused Resolve tether rather than on minion chip. Even or ahead, sustained Danger Zone Flamespitter in a corridor out-damages her poke cycle; behind, play for R and let your team close.

notes: Ability-name error fixed in three places: the page called her root 'RQ' / Mantra-Q. Mantra-Q is a damage cataclysm; the root is Focused Resolve (W) and Mantra-W is what extends it and heals her. Added the two numbers that make this lane playable — Mantra 40/38/36/34 with Gathering Fire shortening it on every landed spell, and Inspire's 10s cooldown replacing a made-up '4 second' shield duration. Also surfaced the tether break (675 range, breaks on distance or line of sight) that the full layer already knew and the content layer never told the player. Level-chart reconciliation: chart gave Karma 6/7 against a 52.3% Rumble win rate; I moved only the 2+ items stage to Rumble, which matches the page's own late-game text, and left her early dominance untouched rather than inventing a shift. Note that win[6] is a one-word field — if the applier's +/-10% length band is applied to it literally the edit will be rejected; the reconciliation is recorded here so the user can make it by hand.
